source.title: Nepal rescuers blast hillside in search of hydropower workers as families wait anxiously
source.summary: Rescuers have resorted to explosives as they struggle to reach trapped workers, as the flooding death toll reaches 939.
source.evidence_text:
In Nepal, flooding left hydropower employees stranded underground in tunnels obstructed by mud.
The search teams used controlled blasts to open a way through the hillside.
Engineers supplied air to the tunnels during the rescue effort.
Relatives of missing staff waited anxiously and called for a quicker rescue.
Chinese and Nepalese military teams led the effort, with specialists from other countries also contributing.
A team entered one tunnel but left after its search there found nobody.
Hydropower is an important part of Nepal’s energy supply.
The floods damaged power projects that were operating as well as others still being built.
An engineer involved in the response described difficulty locating tunnels in the altered landscape.
The power projects employed local workers, migrant workers and specialist engineers.
source.evidence_kind: Editor-written factual notes paraphrased from the linked BBC article; not quotations or independent reporting.
